title: BCIM: A Bit-Serial Approach for Block-Cipher-in-Memory
problem: Existing in-memory block cipher implementations suffer from timing-based side-channel vulnerabilities and energy inefficiency in bit-parallel designs. The challenge is providing both constant-time execution and high-throughput block cipher operations within memory subsystems.
motivation: In-memory cryptography is critical for protecting data in compute-in-memory architectures by enabling efficient encryption/decryption without costly data movement while maintaining resilience against timing attacks.
method: BCIM processes cipher operations one bit at a time rather than in parallel, which naturally takes constant time regardless of input—making it inherently resistant to timing-based side-channel attacks where attackers measure operation duration to deduce secrets. To maintain high speed despite this bit-serial approach, it uses column-wise SIMD processing (single-instruction-multiple-data, where one operation processes multiple data columns simultaneously). The design includes circuit-level optimizations that reduce the memory space needed for storing encryption keys and improve the circuit's operating frequency and power efficiency.
key_novelty: Using bit-serial processing (one bit at a time) alongside column-wise SIMD to achieve both constant-time encryption—which resists timing-based attacks—and high throughput in memory.
contributions: Bit-serial architecture with column-wise SIMD processing for versatile block ciphers in-memory
Inherent constant-time execution providing timing-side-channel attack resilience
Minimal memory footprint design for repetitive key storage with improved peak frequency
Substantial performance and energy efficiency gains over bit-parallel IMC and bitsliced software

metrics.speedup: substantial vs bit-parallel IMC, competitive vs bitsliced software
metrics.energy: orders of magnitude improvement over bitsliced software on CPU/MCU

primary_theme: constant-time in-memory cryptography via bit-serial SIMD
